title: Pin roxygen2 in the pre-commit config
description:
Follow-up to #1300, where the pin was requested.

The pin needs a newer `rev`. `v0.4.3.9025` snapshots a repository without `rdtools`, which roxygen2 8.1.0 requires, so `roxygen2@8.1.0` has no effect there. `v0.4.3.9032` snapshots a later one that has it, and the pin then applies.

Only the {precommit} `rev` is bumped, not the other hooks'. All hooks pass locally, with the `roxygenize` cache cleared so that it actually runs.

title: Fix the pre-commit workflow
description:
Follow-up to comment in #1299. Two unrelated problems, both unrelated to any recent change.

### Cause

The job currently fails in ten seconds, before any hook runs. `sudo apt install` resolves against the runner image's baked-in package index, which pins `libcurl4-openssl-dev 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.13`. Ubuntu has superseded that point release and the mirror no longer carries the deb:

~~~
E: Failed to fetch .../libcurl4-openssl-dev_8.5.0-2ubuntu10.13_amd64.deb  404  Not Found
~~~

With that fixed, the `lintr` hook fails on `R/utils.R:31` with `seq_linter`. The hook installs lintr from `r-lib/lintr`, so it lints against the development version, where #3092 extended `seq_linter()` to `seq(1, n)`. CRAN 3.4.0 does not flag it. `R/utils.R` has not changed since June 2024, so the lint is new rather than the code.

### Fix

Run `apt-get update` before installing, and use `seq_len()` on the flagged line. `ensure_last_n_empty()` returns early when every element is empty, so after `c(x, "", "")` the index is always at least 1 and the empty edge case `seq_linter()` warns about cannot arise. I checked both versions agree across the empty, single-element and all-blank inputs.

`apt-get` in place of `apt` because `apt` warns that its CLI is not stable enough for scripts. `-y` is redundant on GitHub runners, which set `APT::Get::Assume-Yes`, but makes the step correct anywhere.

All 16 hooks pass locally against `--all-files`, and the test suite is unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_, with thorough human review._ Work supported by @GoekeLab.

title: Test function declaration indention at `indent_by = 4`
description:
Follow-up to #1298, which fixed function declaration indention under `indent_by != 2` without a test.

Adds a `test_collection()` pair covering the three cases that were wrong: formals on their own line, the threshold at `2 * indent_by` that separates single from hanging indention, and a nested declaration. The hanging case is included to pin that it is still recognised. All four fail on the commit before #1298 except the hanging one.

title: Forward `indent_by` to the function declaration rules
description:
Fixes #1178. Found through lcolladotor/biocthis#59.

### Cause

`is_single_indent_function_declaration()` decides between single and hanging indention of a function header with the threshold `spaces <= 2 * indent_by`. None of its three callers receive the configured `indent_by`: `unindent_function_declaration()` is stored in the style guide without `partial()`, and `update_indention_reference_function_declaration()` and `remove_line_breaks_in_function_declaration()` have no `indent_by` argument at all. Since `visit_one()` calls each rule with only the parse table, all three fall back to the default of 2.

Thus, with `indent_by = 4`, a header authored with single indention (formals indented by 8) is classified as hanging: `remove_line_breaks_in_function_declaration()` removes the line break after `(`, and `unindent_function_declaration()` indents any remaining formals by 2.

### Fix

Give the two rules that lack it an `indent_by` argument, forward it to `is_single_indent_function_declaration()`, and partialise all three in `tidyverse_style()` like the other indention rules.

```r
foo_4 <- "foo <- function(\n        bar) {\n    NULL\n}"
styler::style_text(foo_4, indent_by = 4)
#> foo <- function(
#>     bar
#> ) {
#>     NULL
#> }
```

Output at `indent_by = 2` is unchanged; the full test suite passes as is. All pre-commit hooks pass.

🤖 Generated with assistance from [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)_, with thorough human review._ Work supported by @GoekeLab.

title: Compatibility with air + housekeeping
description:
~There are surprisingly few conflicts.~ Now, people can format this repo with air and {styler}, with the same output. {styler} is far less invasive than air, so formatting with air once means a lot of code is not changed by {styler} on subsequent styling. 
* Bug in air: https://github.com/posit-dev/air/issues/499 caused a re-naming for convenience here. 
* multi-line assignment is handled differently by {styler} than air, this can be circumvented by making sure the first line break in the statement does not occur directly after `<-`.
* {styler} forced no line break after first argument in `switch()`. This was relaxed for compatibility with air.
* We used `fmt: skip` in `switch()` statements to make the pre-commit hook pass.
* ~air does not respect the tidyverse rules which allow to keep unnamed argument on the first line~ This rule seems removed. it turns: 
  ```r
  map(x, f, 
    arg = 1, 
    arg = 2
  )
  ``` 
  Into
  ```
  map(
    x, 
    f, 
    arg = 1, 
    arg = 2
  )
  ```
  Which I think is not optimal.

* Another case is
  ```r
    other_trigger_on_same_line <- (
      pd$token[remaining_row_idx_between_trigger_and_line_break] %in%
        other_trigger_tokens
    )
  ```
  becomes (with air)
  ```r
    other_trigger_on_same_line <- (pd$token[
      remaining_row_idx_between_trigger_and_line_break
    ] %in%
      other_trigger_tokens)
  ```
  Where I also think {styler} styles superior.

* It could not preserve alignment in the blow snippet
  ```r
  style_guide_name <- "styler::tidyverse_style@https://github.com/r-lib"
      create_style_guide(
        # transformer functions
        initialize             = default_style_guide_attributes,
        line_break             =        line_break_manipulators,
        space                  =             space_manipulators,
        token                  =             token_manipulators,
        indention              =         indention_manipulators,
        ...
      )
  ```
* it broke a lot of long lines, which I think is desirable. This increased the line count of the source code.
* Only single lines can be ignored, no ranges: https://github.com/posit-dev/air/issues/456.

title: Include Positron Extension in third-party integration list
Cleaner stack trace with visitors
description:
- Ensures that all visited functions have a name
- This name now appears in the stack trace thanks to `make_visit_one()`

We could extend this idea to implementing a `make_visit()` function, `pre_visit()` would be `visitor <- make_visit(pre = TRUE)` then `visitor(pd_nested)` . This would save a few function calls, give more compact code, and also better stack traces for `pre_visit_one()` (which would vanish). The 80-20 rule forbids to do this right now, maybe later. Also, this turns the whole visiting logic into a metaprogram, this is a slippery slope.

For #759.

title: stylerignore sequences must always be in one block
description:
With this PR, styling is correct for a stylerignore sequence that contains a cached expression. The solution involves ensuring that a stylerignore sequence is always processed in one block. Closes #1072. 

``` r
full <- c(
  '# styler: off',
  'skip_if_not_installed("tibble")',
  'local({',
  'x<-1',
  '})',
  '# styler: on'
)
without_ignore <- full[c(-1, -length(full))]
styler:::local_test_setup(cache = TRUE)
styler:::style_text(without_ignore)
#> skip_if_not_installed("tibble")
#> local({
#>   x <- 1
#> })
styler:::style_text(full)
#> # styler: off
#> skip_if_not_installed("tibble")
#> local({
#> x<-1
#> })
#> # styler: on
```

<sup>Created on 2022-12-26 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: Check if all examples run successfully
description:
`\donttest` examples are run in [an additional check](https://www.stats.ox.ac.uk/pub/bdr/donttest/) by BDR, and probably `\dontrun` examples are also run in some other checks. 

Therefore, making sure all examples run successfully (or are never run if they are just for illustrative purposes) is a good preventive practice in general. 

This PR does that and also adds a workflow to catch such failures in the future.

title: Improve a few function names
description: We are being unnecessarily terse in some places where we don't need to be. I always feel like I am hitting a little speed bump every time I need to decode these names mentally.

title: Use `expect_no_warning()`
description:
Instead of `expect_warning()` + `NA` combo.

Automated via:

```r
replace_multiline <- function(dir = "tests/") {
  files <- list.files(dir, pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
  
  pattern <- "(?s)expect_warning\\((.*?)\\,\\s*NA\\)"
  replacement <- "expect_no_warning(\\1)"
  
  for (f in files) {
    txt <- xfun::read_utf8(f)
    content <- paste(txt, collapse = "\n")
    new_content <- gsub(pattern, replacement, content, perl = TRUE)
    
    if (!identical(content, new_content)) {
      new_txt <- unlist(strsplit(new_content, "\n", fixed = TRUE))
      xfun::write_utf8(new_txt, f)
      message("Modified: ", f)
    }
  }
  
  invisible(NULL)
}

replace_multiline("tests/")
```

title: Use stable version of `{purrr}`

``` r
internal_map_dfr <- function(.x, .f, ...) {
  .f <- purrr::as_mapper(.f, ...)
  res <- purrr::map(.x, .f, ...)
  vctrs::vec_rbind(!!!res)
}

x <- list(
  a = data.frame(x = rnorm(1e6)),
  b = data.frame(y = rnorm(1e6))
)

bench::mark(
  internal_map_dfr(x, ~ .x),

)
```

Bumps [JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action](https://github.com/jamesives/github-pages-deploy-action) from 4.6.4 to 4.6.8.
Release notes

Sourced from JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action's releases.

v4.6.8

What's Changed

Bug Fixes 🐝

  • fix: :bug: Added the temp deployment directory created by the action to the git safe directory list. This resolves an issue in certain circumstances where the deployment would fail depending on the types of files moved around by the workflow - #1694.
  • fix: Resolved a rare deployment error where the action would complain that origin/${branch_name} is not a commit and a branch cannot be created from it. The action will continue to attempt to track the origin branch, but if this step fails, it will create a new untracked branch to continue the deployment from. - #1689.

Testing 🧪

  • test: 🧪 Improved the integration test suite so it now runs immediately post-release to ensure that any issues do no longer in the major version tag (ie @v4). This was done to combat problems raised by #1697.

title: Don't store code tree structures in tests
description:
Closes #1206

And also remove everything that was needed for R 3.2.

Script used to delete files:

```r
tree_files_to_delete <-
  fs::dir_ls(
    path = ".",
    glob = "*.R|*.Rprofile|*.Rmd|*.Rmarkdown|*.Rnw|*.Qmd",
    invert = TRUE,
    type = "file",
    recurse = TRUE
  ) |>
  stringr::str_subset("_tree") |>
  purrr::map_chr(fs::path_abs)

stopifnot(all(fs::file_exists(tree_files_to_delete)))

fs::file_delete(tree_files_to_delete)
```

In scope of this release, we update node version runtime from node16 to node20 (actions/setup-python#772). Besides, we update dependencies to the latest versions.

steps:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: actions/setup-python@v4 
  with:
    python-version: 'graalpy-22.3' 
- run: python my_script.py

title: Fix CRAN warning on invalid numeric version inputs
description:
> This is about the "invalid non-character version specification" errors
for r-devel-linux-x86_64-debian-gcc.
R-devel has been warning about invalid (non-character) numeric version
inputs for some time now, but such warnings typically go unnoticed, so
at least for the time being, one can get errors instead of warnings by
setting _R_CHECK_STOP_ON_INVALID_NUMERIC_VERSION_INPUTS_=true.
In your case, 
assert_transformers <- function(transformers) {

title: Check benchmarks only with rlang bump
Bump benchmark config
description:
@IndrajeetPatil Seems like `try_fetch()` got a lot faster recently. When I made a benchmark run, it was much faster than `with_handlers()`:
``` r
library(rlang)
bench::mark(
  rlang::with_handlers({}, error = function(...) NULL),
  rlang::try_fetch({}, error = function(...) NULL),
)
#> Warning: `with_handlers()` is deprecated as of rlang 1.0.0.
#> ℹ Please use `tryCatch()`, `withCallingHandlers()`, or `try_fetch()`.
#> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression                                                 min  median itr/s…¹
#>   <bch:expr>                                            <bch:tm> <bch:t>   <dbl>
#> 1 rlang::with_handlers({ }, error = function(...) NULL)   6.37ms  6.47ms    152.
#> 2 rlang::try_fetch({ }, error = function(...) NULL)      10.75µs 11.62µs  84532.
#> # … with 2 more variables: mem_alloc <bch:byt>, `gc/sec` <dbl>, and abbreviated
#> #   variable name ¹​`itr/sec`
```

<sup>Created on 2023-04-04 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>


I am bumping the benchmarking deps here, let's see what they bring and then, you can rebase #1103 on main to see if the problem persists.

``` r
  {
    x
  }, error = function(e) e
)")
#> tryCatch({
#>   x
#> }, error = function(e) e)
```

<sup>Created on 2019-09-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

While at the same time, preserve formatting of `testthat()` expressions:

``` r
styler::style_text("testthat(x, {
  code(to(exec))
})")
#> testthat(x, {
#>   code(to(exec))
#> })
```

<sup>Created on 2019-09-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

The abstract rule was formulated in https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/428#issuecomment-473192227. 
> Function arguments that consist of a braced expression always need to start on a new line, unless it's the last argument and all other arguments fit on the line of the function call or they are named.

The last part of the sentence *or they are named.* is needed for this case:
```r
testthat(x, 
  b = 
  {
    5
})
```
 
Where we should rearrange to
```r
testthat(x, 
  b = {
  5
})
```

Closes #428.

title: correct cache invalidation for include_roxygen_examples and base_indention
description:
This PR introduces a new concept for caching: `more_args` In addition to the text and the transformers that determine cache invalidation, there are currently two arguments in styler APIs that are not part of the style guide that determine styling:

- `include_roxygen_examples`: determines whether or not roxygen code examples are styled or not.
- `base_indention` as introduced in #649, determines the global indention of all supplied code. 

These two arguments need to be propagated down to the functions that determine if code is cached and if not, write to the cache. I am not sure if it's a good idea to introduce `base_indention` because it requires significant amount of additional code (this PR and #649) and has very limited use cases and may slow styler down (needs to be investigated). However, even without it, #654 is something we had to fix anyways I believe (unless we want to make the restriction that `include_roxygen_examples = FALSE` is incompatible with the cache usage, which I think we should not), so we pass two arguments instead of one into `more_specs`, that's pretty much it.

title: Cache styling
description:
Closes #320. 

# Goal

The goal is to make styler remember what it styled so the pre-commit hook in https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/pre-commit-hooks is much faster and functions like `styler::style_pkg()` are much faster if run on already styled files.

# Requirements

The requirements are:

* must work on all plattforms and must not be error-prone.

* the user should be able to manage it (know its size and location, deactivate,
  clear, delete)

* should be as close to the functionality "once seen, by style_text(), Addin or
  style_file() remembered forever".

* The cache should be default be enabled, but the required packages should be in
  `Suggests` to keep the core installation lightweight. If `R.cache` is not
  installed, we should issue a warning message, deactivate the caching feature
  for the current R session and ask the user to install the dependencies and or
  permanently disable the feature in their .Rprofile with
  usethis::edit_r_profile().

* For this reason, the styling should also work when `R.cache` is not installed,
  which requires every `R.cache` call to be wrapped in a conditional.

* The advanced user should be able to understand how R.cache was used to
  implement the caching.

# Conceputal

In this PR we introduce caching to styler. We follow the approach outlined in
https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/320#issuecomment-520747381, which basically is:

* check if text to style is in cache.

* if not, style it and add styled text to cache.

The approach has the following advantages:

* Very simple to implement.

* API agnostic. Works for files, text, Addin because it operates on the text
  level, which is quite low level.

* Because approach is path and modification time independent, it can cache the
  same content in different locations, including renaming, copies in multiple
  places as well as moving files. Can cache multiple versions of a file, e.g. on
  different branches, when going back and forth in the git history.

* Cache remains very small because no actual code is cached.

The cache must be styler version specific because if not, updated styling rules
won't be applied.

# Implementation

* We use `R.cache` to power the caching.

* We use R options to manage it, with additional functional wrappers to modify
  the options.

  DESCRIPTION.

* We modify `.travis.yaml` to also test behavior if `R.cache` is not installed.

title: Remove unused transformers before processing
description:
Some transformers like the one turning `a;b` -> `a\nb` are rarely used, as the token `;` rarely ocurrs in data. But we apply the associated transformer `force_assignment_op()` on every nest, knowing in advance that we'll never use it. This is expensive. There are quite some transformers that we know will be used infrequently. The idea of this PR is to extend `create_style_guide()` to take a new ~`subset_transformer`~ `transformers_drop` argument, which is a list that contains the names of the transformers and which token must be missing for the rule to be included in the final set of transformers used:
```r
transformers_drop <- list(
    force_assignment_op = "EQ_ASSIGN",
    add_line_break_after_pipe = "SPECIAL-PIPE",
    wrap_if_else_while_for_fun_multi_line_in_curly = c("IF", "WHILE", "FOR", "FUNCTION"),
    ...
)
``` 
If the parse table contains no `EQ_ASSIGN` token for example, the `force_asignment_op` transformer will be removed from the set of transformers before these are applied at every **nest**.

Idea originated in https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/558#issuecomment-542883365.

title: Line break after pipe
description:
This PR implements the rule that `%>%` must *usually* be followed by a new line. 99% of the cases are: 
```r
blue %>% green() 
# is turned into
blue %>%
  green()
```

Exceptions are various constellations within function calls. This is discouraged practice anyways but we don't want to make things worse
```r
call(a, b %>% c())

# won't be turned into
call(
  a, b %>% 
    c()
)
# or similar
```
See test files added in this PR for more examples.

Reason: It's not non-invasive and comes at a technically high cost (relatively large slow-down for edge case), more complex code.

```r
call(d = g(b) %>% 
  c)
```

should probably be turned into

```r
call(
  d = g(b) %>% 
    c
)
```
But it is not, again because of the same reasons. A more natural choice would be 
```r
call(d = g(b) %>% c)
```
in many cases. 

This closes #470.

title: Granular scope selection
description:
Closes #703. 

Context: When `use_raw_indention` is `TRUE` (which it is when `scope < 'indention'` prior to this PR), the number of spaces between tokens on different lines is applied after the line break to restore initial indention. For that reason, spaces between tokens on different lines **must not** be modified in any case, otherwise `scope < 'indention'` would not work properly anymore. You can see that pretty much all transformers under `R/rules-spacing.R` don't modify `spaces` without checking for `newlines == 0L`. Indention is tracked separately in the column `indention` and then applied at the end with `choose_indention()` if `use_raw_indention` is `FALSE`, otherwise, `lag_spaces` is used.

*** 

For some reason not obvious to me at this moment, all indention transformers were grouped under the space transformers in `tidyverse_style` at the beginning, except `update_indention_ref_fun_dec()` is listed under `indention` transformers (probably because it must come after all spacing rules). However, one could try to move all indention rules from the spaces transformers *before* `update_indention_ref_fun_dec()` and see if things pass.

Also, these rules live in `R/indent.R`, and not `R/rules-indention.R` (which does not exist), where they should be for consistency with other rules like spacing (but `R/rules-replacment.R` and `R/rules-other.R` is also not consistent...). 

These concerns were addressed in #707.

description:
Closes #551 by implementing the suggested solution outlined in https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/551#issuecomment-540788608. Put that into a file and style it with styler, all `\` should be preserved, only quotes should be replaced (does not work well with reprex).
```

'here
is a string
'
'here\nis a string
'
'here\\nis a string'

```

Note that for mixing the invisible line break and \n in single quotes, we leave it as is (second example).

title: indent deeply-nested EQ_FORMALS correctly
description:
# Problem

**non-technical:** When nested deeper than 1 level, indention of function headers is generally not correct: 
``` r
styler::style_text('MyClass <- R6::R6Class(
    "MyClass",
    public = list(initialize = function(my_arg,
                                        my_named_arg = 1) {
        return(invisible())
      }
    ),
  )')
#> MyClass <- R6::R6Class(
#>   "MyClass",
#>   public = list(initialize = function(my_arg,
#>                                         my_named_arg = 1) {
#>     return(invisible())
#>   }),
#> )
```

<sup>Created on 2019-09-23 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

**technical source:** In `apply_ref_indention_one()`, the parse table is already flat, the indention of all tokens is absolute. However, for those where indention should be copied from another token, their indention must be relative, otherwise we'll double account for some indention.

See this exceprt from `R/reindent.R`, `apply_ref_indention_one()`:
```r
copied_spaces <- flattened_pd$col2[target_token]  # contains already absolute indention
shift <- copied_spaces
  flattened_pd$lag_spaces[token_to_update] <-
    flattened_pd$lag_spaces[token_to_update] + # contains also absolute indention
    shift
  # in sum, we have indention twice, hence, we must make sure that when flattened out,
  # the token that get their indention from another token contain relative indention.
 
```
Formals need to be aligned with the absolute indention of the opening brace. If you add another time their absolute indention, they will be indented way to much.

# Solution

When flattening the parse table, keep the indention level of all tokens that have a ref_pos_id relative, so when added with an absolute indention in `apply_ref_indention()`, it will become absolute indention. Closes #541.

title: Caching top level expressions
description:
The cache is currently invalidated if any expression is modified. If we manage to cache top level expressions separately, we can still use the cache for all non-modified expressions, which would should improve speed very often. Closes #570. 

- [x] Do only add variables block and is_cached (if at all) after than
  get_parse_data (but before parse_transform_serialize_r_block because when we
  do block processing this might be too late) to not drag along
  transformers everywhere totally unrelated. When processing blocks, make sure
  to cache individual values where they are created.

- [x] process in block, not every expression.

- [x] expressions on the same line must be processed together, i.e. when separated
  by semi-colon or comment, they belong to the same block.

- [x] think about the interaction with create_tokens and that each column should
  potentially exist on every level, not just top level.

- [x] the text attibute of a top level nest is not used to create a hash for
  caching, but is used to return text in case no styling is needed because the
  value is cached.

- [x] resolve line break problem.

- [x] Add tests. Both low-level and high-level.

- [x] `compute_parse_data_nested()` should not compute the parse data nested for expressions that are cached already because for them, we just return `text` of the top level expression.

- [x] Put all consecutive non-cached expressions into one block to speed up things. Maybe this does not help as much as expected. Need more comprehensive benchmarks.

- [x] ~nice to have: Cache after styling each expression separately, so styling a
  file with ten identical expressions will use cache for 9 of them.~ Does not seem to work because we must have blocks first.

Note: The diff is so large because all trees are rewritten as we use `includeText = TRUE` in `getParseData()`. Otherwise it would be 5k lower.

title: Switch to lorenzwalthert/touchstone
description:
This PR replaces the continuous benchmarking infrastructure provided by r-lib/bench with the [touchstone](https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/touchstone) package. Key insights were:

* Does not make sense to only benchmark the feature branch, but benchmark the base branch as well and look at *relative difference* because two CI/CD runs are not exactly comparable in terms of available compute power. This matters in particular when running one iteration of a benchmark takes long (>> a few seconds) and speed implications are small.
* Maintaining a timeline such as the implementation of r-lib/bench is of limited use because of the first bullet. Speed implications are to be checked between two revisions.
* R and package versions must be fixed via RSPM to allow as much continuation as possible anyways. Changing the timestamp of RSPM can happen in PRs that are only dedicated to dependency updates.

From https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/touchstone.

First results with 20 iterations are promising and take about 30 minutes. They show 0% difference in median for this PR, which was expected as no code that is benchmarked changes. Second run: 0.9%, third run 3%, fourth -0.1%. Results can be found under the GitHub Action -> Artifacts.

Here is the comparison of 20 iterations with 20 times `style_pkg()` for the `here` package for master and touchstone branch.

![density](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10477073/100203200-94ee0900-2f02-11eb-8a4d-25c3cdc80d45.png)

``` r
library(magrittr)
  library(styler)
  text_long <- c(
    "#' Roxygen",
    "#' Comment",
    "#' @examples",
    "#' 1 + 1",
    "#' if (x > 4)",

    "#' call(x,y=2)",

    "    k()",
    "  }",

  )
  text_long_styled <- style_text(text_long)
  purrr::map_dbl(1:5,
    function(x) {
      styler:::fresh_testthat_cache()
      text_long_styled <- style_text(text_long)
      text_long_styled[13] <- "    }"
      system.time(style_text(text_long_styled))['elapsed']
  }) %>%
    mean()
```

title: Ignore certain lines when styling
description:
Closes #365 as well as it's duplicates #533 and #542, following the https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/365#issuecomment-541216912. Here is a short example of how to use it, it works both for segments as well as inline:
```r
call(1 ) # styler: off
# styler: off
# also if there are more comments
test_xkj("hier", na.rm = 3, py = 43
         )

x="new" # styler: off
y=1 # none

more_calls(with(arguments))
# styler: on
1 + 1
a(!b)
```


Taken from the outline in #365, this PR implements the functionality as follows:

Here is how to make sure this code does not get styled: 

* Before parse data is nested, we find the stylerignore tags and add a column 
  stylerignore to the parse data which is false for all token except the 
  tokens that fall between two stylerignore tags.

* After code is turned into nested parse data and spaces and newlines are 
  computed (must be between terminals, not between any token as currently done with 
  `default_style_guilde_attributes()` **edit:** Because we need the position of tokens relative to other terminals, not tokens in general when serializing, we must do   `default_style_guilde_attributes()` twice in total now). We store the lag_spaces and 
  lag_newline attributes for all terminal tokens that are marked as 
  stylerignore in the environment env_current.
* We proceed as usual with appyling transformers and flattening out the parse 
  table. 
* Right before we serialize the parse table, we replace lag_newlines, lag_spaces
  and tokens, text with the initial values for all tokens that were marked as 
  stylerignore. Then we serialize.

title: Fix style_file() so it works for a vector of files from different directories
description:
Closes #521 by not changing working directory to directory where the file lays. The bug was long undetected because `setwd()` fails silently on a character vector within `withr::with_dir()` and is particularly relevant for #467, e.g. when R files in `R/` and `tests/testthat` are staged simultaneously.

Note that this is an **API change** in the sense that now, the path to the directory where the files lay are printed, not just the file names, which also affects the invisible return values of the stylers that contain the path.
``` r
withr::with_dir(
  "~/datasciencecoursera/styler", {
    out <- styler::style_file(c("R/utils-files.R", "tests/testthat/strict/strict-out.R"))
    out
  }
)
#> Styling  2  files:
#>  R/utils-files.R                    ✔ 
#>  tests/testthat/strict/strict-out.R ✔ 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────
#> Status   Count   Legend 
#> ✔    2   File unchanged.
#> ℹ    0   File changed.
#> ✖    0   Styling threw an error.
#> ────────────────────────────────────────
#> # A tibble: 2 x 2
#>   file                               changed
#>   <chr>                              <lgl>  
#> 1 R/utils-files.R                    FALSE  
#> 2 tests/testthat/strict/strict-out.R FALSE
```

<sup>Created on 2019-06-19 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

This change has implications for testing also. To make a comparison with an exact expectation, in the tests, we temporarily change the working directory to keep file paths and ruler width (that depends on the path) identical on all platforms. See `?styler:::catch_style_file_output`. Testing for the `cat()` outputs of the public API was refactored also in this PR.

The new utility `rds_to_version()` can be used to convert rds objects to the old serialization format to ensure CI passing. They are introduced in this PR because this is a use case where we need to udpate current reference values. Closes #524.

title: return() on newline
description:
This PR makes `return()` statements going to a new line and hence closes #473. They are already always on a new line with the current implementation of `tidyverse_style()`, the only exception occurs in conjunction with a conditional statement, as described in #473. For this reason, the rule to be implemented is not a line break rule. Because all line break rules do separate expressions that *could* also go on one line like `{1}` or `x %>% y()` but the requirements for #473 are different. Implementing as a line break rule leads to a lot of headake as described in #473 because it had to be as follows:

* Implement line break rule for `return()`.
* Fix edge case in conjunction with if statement. When wrapping an expression in curly braces, check if it contains `return()` and then remove the line break right at the `return` token. However, finding `return()` might be non-trivial because you can also almost always have `COMMENT` tokens in the parse table.

This results in a lot of code and additional complexity (I tried it). Instead, we modify the behavior of `wrap_if_else_multi_line_in_curly()` (renamed) to *always* wrap the if statement in curly braces when it contains `return()`. In addition, this approach lets us easily wrap for and while loop statement into braces too, using a `key_token` that indicates for each of the cases (if, for, while loop) which tokens helps identifying the expression to wrap into curly braces (ignoring comments). Apart from this, this PR is unfortunately convoluted with some clean-up, documentation improvement and re-location of function declarations between files. Hence, this PR closes #286.

This PR also includes the renaming of `wrap_if_else_while_for_multi_line_in_curly)` in the tidyverse style guide, which some people might rely on because it is the output of an exported function.

title: Adapt to R devel parser
description:
Closes #419. We need to distinguish two cases: Before the parser fix outlined in #419 was committed into R devel and afterwards. The parser version is identified from the parse data. If the parse data contains an `equal_assign` token, we know it's the second case and say the parser version is `2`. If not, we don't know, because parse data for all expressions not involving `EQ_ASSIGN` can't be distinguished, so we just assume it is version `1`. 
I propose to use an environment to store specifications about the current run, i.e. to store the parser version. I am not sure if that's a good idea. But since we need to have the parser version available in different places, I can't think of a better way. Also, I am not sure about using version numbers for the parser and if it is a good idea to derive the parser version from the result of parsing. An alternative approach is to base it on the `Rversion` number, but that's a bit brittle I think. Any comments on that @krlmlr?

title: remove spaes after !! and !!!
description:
Closes #321 but does even more because it also remove the space after`!!!`. It seems not so easy to distinguish `!!` and `!!!` since they are on separate levels in the nested parse table and we only have `token_before` and `token_after`, but we also needed `token_before2` and `token_after2` which does not seem to be particularly elegant. An alternative is go inside the child to see what comes afterwards, and set the spacing before processing the child. Also not very nice. Maybe let's remove the space after both `!!` and `!!!` for now.
``` r
styler:::create_tree("call(!!!a)")
#>                                                  levelName
#> 1  ROOT (token: short_text [lag_newlines/spaces] {pos_id})
#> 2   °--expr:  [0/0] {1}                                   
#> 3       ¦--expr:  [0/0] {3}                               
#> 4       ¦   °--SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL: call [0/0] {2}       
#> 5       ¦--'(': ( [0/0] {4}                               
#> 6       ¦--expr:  [0/0] {5}                               
#> 7       ¦   ¦--'!': ! [0/0] {6}                           
#> 8       ¦   °--expr:  [0/0] {7}                           
#> 9       ¦       ¦--'!': ! [0/0] {8}
```

title: Fix indention in if-else statement
description:
`compute_indent_indices()` assumed that if the nest expression contains `(`, the closing `)` is always the last token, which is not true for if-else clauses. For that reason, everything between `(` and the last token got indented.
``` r
styler::style_text("{if (TRUE)\n1\nelse\n2\n}")
#> {
#>   if (TRUE)
#>     1
#>     else
#>     2
#> }
```
Now, the closing token can be supplied and located. Consequentially indention can be done for all tokens between the opening and the closing token. Closes #191.

title: Re-indent token-dependent
description:
This is the fourth part of #106 and it is revised significantly. This PR closes #99 and closes #66 by allowing token-dependent re-indention. This is achieved by using the visitor to add references to tokens if necessary. Tokens that don't need re-indention have `NA`s in the corresponding reference column. The reference is propagated to the terminals. Once the parse table is flattened out and the position of every token is defined in terms of `line1`, `line2`, `col1`, `col2`, the indention of reference token is applied to the token that should inherit the indention from the reference token and the corresponding attributes in the parse table are updated.

A transformer function that breaks lines for long function calls as suggested in the [tidyverse style guide](http://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#long-lines) is not yet pushed to this branch. It seems rather invasive compared to the other rules. Nevertheless, I think we should include it. I was just not sure about the concrete implementation and opened #118.

"spaces" will not modify indention anymore (closes #104, closes #105). Note that since we use named transformers in R/transform.R (because depending on what is modified, the transformer needs to be called at a certain point in the process), we can also use values other than functions in the transformers. I think that's a natural extension plus since the parse table is already flattened out, I think this cannot be done well with a transformer function.

title: Fix eq assign parsing
description:
Closes #259. As outlined in #259, we

* Walk all nests
* Within one nest, we split the nest into sub-nests that contain one assignment expression (e.g. `a = b = c`) at most.
* Within every such sub-nest, we relocate the assignment expression.

However, we only do that if there is an `EQ_ASSIGN` token in the flat parse data since the whole procedure is rather costly and we can expect the probability that there is an `EQ_ASSIGN` in the parse data to be small.

Add tools for re-indenting tokens that match certain regular expression patterns, in particular, to allow strcode code separators. Closes #64, but is actually much more general. The indention level for an arbitrary token text that matches any regular expression in the regex vector passed to the styling function can be controlled. One absolute indention level for all matches in one run can be set. But probably no one would like to do that actually.

See `tests/testthat/unindention_regex/random_non_comment_indention-out.R` to see the how the indention level for the token `bbx` was set to 5. This function call that lead to this result can be found in `tests/testthat/unindention_regex/random_non_comment_indention-out.R`

title: Math token spacing
description:
This PR gives granular control over spacing around math tokens, as envisioned in #82 and requested in https://github.com/tidyverse/lubridate/pull/577#issuecomment-331700557.  
Implements a new paradigm for transformer functions in the sense that `strict` is now an argument to
the transformer. This reduces duplication of code, since the only part that `set_*` and `add_*` functions for spacing rules are different is that `set_*` uses `pd_flat$spaces[...] <- level` wherease `add_*` uses `pd_flat$spaces[...] <- pmax(1, pd_flat$spaces[...]`.
Functions that follow this paradigm should be named `style_*` instead of `add_*` and `set_*`.
`pd_flat` is the last argument to `style_space_around_math_token()` because this allows using `purrr::partial()` without naming arguments.

title: Remove outdated line and col information
description:
Now that we have closed #112, we could remove the col and line columns. The only problem is that we need to preserve the number of empty lines before the start of any content, which was done using `line1` so far. One way is to extract the starting line from the nested parse table, do the processing pass the number of blank lines to serialization function. 
Alternatively, we could add a start token at the top level of the nest, but that brings additional trouble: We'd have to check in every spacing rule that the token before is not the start token, otherwise we will add spaces before certain tokens, e.g. "{}" will become "   {}". I think that's less elegant.

I also thought about adding the start line as an attribute to the parse table, but it seems that keeping the attribute attached to the parse table through all transformations is not necessarily more elegant.

This PR closes #147. 

Note that in `enrich_terminals()`, the updated line and col information is added again.

For example we change



All other top-level stylers such as `style_dir()`, `style_pkg()` etc. are also adapted to be consistent with the example above. Second argument is always `...`.

title: Token dependent indention
description:
This PR consists of two parts:

**Step 1: Allow for token-dependent indention**
This implements #94 (and hence #66) rudimentary. By flattening out the nested parse table completely and computing the absolute position a token will take when serialised, we can use a look-up approach to set the indention of any token dependent on the indention of another token. There is room for improvement since `set_token_dependent_indention()` is really just work in progress and can be improved.

**Step 2: Allow for styling without touching indention**
Since step 1 implies to merge the spacing and indention information in `enrich_terminals()`into the column `spaces`, we are also able to discard the indention computed and use what we called raw indention, that is, take the indention from the input and don't modify it. The only thing for it to work is to not overwrite the spacing information if there is a line break after a token, which is checked via `newlines`. Since we modify `lag_newlines` before (in R/rules-line_breaks.R) and not `newlines`, this attribute needs to be updated after line breaks are set (closes #104). Hence, step 2 closes #105 and lays the foundations for #85.

title: Tidy rules
description:
This PR is WIP, it's not yet intended to be merged and some points need further
discussion.

## Content of PR
So far, styler did essentially one thing. Adding and removing spaces between
tokens within one line. With this PR, styler is extended to also add and remove
line breaks between the tokens. Concretely, we add

* line breaks according to the tidyverse style guide, section [2.4](http://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#indenting). I could not really produce valid R code where there was something else than a closing bracket after a closing curly bracket, so there is no rule that forces a line break after a closing curly bracket.
* assignment operator `<-` replaces equal assignment `=` as in section [2.6](http://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#assignment).
* Semicolons are removed and statements are put on a new line as section [2.7](http://style.tidyverse.org/syntax.html#semicolons) requires.
* Pipes `%>%` cause a line break as section [4.2](http://style.tidyverse.org/pipes.html#spacing-and-indenting) states.
* Brackets are added to function calls without arguments and no parentheses if they are chained by a pipe, as section [4.3](http://style.tidyverse.org/pipes.html#no-arguments) requires.

For those changes, it is essential to place the line break information on the
right level of nesting. Otherwise, another round of styling will add add
another line break since styler thinks that there is none yet.

Relating to #36, the text-to-token-mapping was slightly modified, that is,
all text that had token SPECIAL (like `%>%` or `%in%`) now map to a unique
identifier (like "SPECIAL-PIPE", or "SPECIAL-IN") or to the fall-back class
("SPECIAL-OTHER"). This is required as for example `%>%` should be followed
by a line break whereas we don't want to force a line break after `%in%`. It's
also necessary to add brackets to function calls in pipes as stated by the last
bullet point above.

## Remaining problems

### `line1`/ `line2`
A new problem coming up with manipulating line break information relates to
operations that use the (not updated) line information `line1` and `line2` -
notably the functions that create indention. Before, `indention_needed()`
checks whether there is a sub-expression within the parse table that starts
on the same line as the expression in the parse table but does not stop on
the very same line. If that was the case, no indention was needed. This check
was implemented by comparing `line1` and `line2`.

One way to go about that would be to base the check upon `lag_newlines`, but I
think this is quite expensive as we needed to check *recursively* whether *any*
of the sub-expressions has `lag_newline` > 0.
Another would be to change `line1` and `line2` while updating `lag_newlines`
and still use the *old* approach. Can't tell how well that would work accros
levels of nesting, since for example with `if (x < 3) { 2 } else { 4 }`, it's
not just moving one token from one line to the other, it is essentially moving
all children after the first opening parenthesis one line below, so for the
closing parenthesis etc. Maybe we can just update them on one level of nesting
and hope that will work? This seems more of a hack though.
Another not apprach
that is not very elegant either is to first do flat styling for line-breaks
only, write back and then read in again to do the nested styling.

@krlmlr do you see other options?

### Backward compatibility of flat approach
92129249 in rules-spacing.R changes `set_space_after_comma()` so spaces after
a comma are set to one. The space was previously only set to one if there was
no line break after the comma. This condition was dropped since now we may
rearrange the line breaks and we may remove the line-break. However, this
means that initial indention is not preserved for these cases anymore (for the
flat approach). Changing the order of the transformer functions to first
modify the line breaks would not help much since all spacing rules (written by
@krlmlr for the flat approch initialy) are based on the column `newlines`, not
`lag_newliens`. Maybe we should eventually consider rewriting these rules anyways to be
based on `lag_newlines` since I think there is no other dependency on
`newlines` apart from these rules, so we could simplify things and get rid of
this column.

title: add function to style a single .R file. Closes #27.
Transform nested
description:
## Content of PR
* `get_transformers()` calls either `get_transformers_flat()` or `get_transformers_nested()`. We use `purrr::partial()` so the user can pre-fill arguments such as `indent_by` of `indent_round()` when  `get_transformers_nested()` is called.
* introducing the visitor concept: Not every transformation such as `create_filler()` or `indent_round()` is carried out going through the whole hierarchy. Rather, the visitor applies all transformer functions on one level before going one level deeper and applying them there.
* Adding top-level argument `flat` to `style_text()` et al.
* adapting initial tests with in.R/ out.R to use `flat = TRUE` so they all pass.

## Questions

Currently, the user can use `flat` at the top-level functions to use either the flat or the nested styling approach and `get_transformers()` will have `flat = flat` by default. If the user wants to use a non-default value in `get_transformers()`, he or she needs to specify `flat` twice, i.e. as in tests/testthat/test-styler#17, 
```r
style_text("file_in.R")),
    flat = TRUE,
    transformers = get_transformers(flat = TRUE, strict = FALSE))
```
This is the case since we must know 

* which functions are the transformer functions to be used. We need `create_filler` et al. in addition to the rules in R/rules.R for `flat = FALSE`.
* which procedure should be applied when doing the transformations (nested or flat).

I don't see a better way to do that at the moment. I think we can leave it for now since eventually, the flat argument will be obsolete anyways or at least people will just use the default `flat = FALSE` mostly. Should we leave it like that for now @krlmlr?

## To do's (regarding transformations):
* use visitor concept for tests also.

title: No line break after switch and friends
description:
As requested in https://github.com/krlmlr/rlang/pull/1#discussion_r134582400, it is now possible to not break the line in function calls where the text of the function is in `except_text_before`. I.e.
```r
switch(x, 
  z, 
  y
)
```
Will not be turned into 
```r
switch(
  x, 
  z, 
  y
)
```

Since there is no such rule in the tidyverse style guide yet, I suggest opening an issue or PR before merging this. 
Also, I am not sure whether the names of the functions should be an argument to `tidyverse_style()`. For now, they are not. `case_when()` might also be such a function that should be treated as an exception.

title: Use multi line
description:
In the main, this PR refines `needs_indention()` and `set_unindention_child()` (as proposed in #76) such that we do no longer rely on `line1`/ `line2`, which is a problem because as introduced by #71, we do now modify line breaks but don't update `line1`/ `line2`. The problem is described in detail in #71. The solution is the creation of a multi-line attribute as proposed in #75 through a post-visitor after the line break rules were applied.
Linked to this, the transformers are now grouped into the following groups as suggested in #73:

* space modifiers
* Line break modifiers
* token modifiers

Plus they were rearranged (#77) so we first modify line breaks, then compute the multi-line attribute, then modify spaces and tokens.

title: Indent with renesting
description:
This pull request addresses two linked topics:

* The more complex topic is indention based on operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%>%` etc. To solve this
  problem, I first had to add a function that changes the nested structure of the parse table. 
  This function rearranges the parse table so that elements between these infix operators are 
  on the same level of nesting. Also see the commit description in 613fb5e or the help files
  `re_nest()`, `move_children_up()`. I did not see a way of doing that differently while getting
  all edge cases right.

* correctly handle unary operators. The function that worked on the flat parse table does not work
  with the nested structure, so I created a new one. However, so far, the transformers for the 
  nested structure was just the transformers for the flat structure and some special transformers 
  for the nested structure. That is no longer true since this flat transformer is not needed on the 
  nested structure. How should we handle that? I mean eventually we can delete them anyways.

A remaining topic is indention in situations where we have both braces and parenthesis.
```r
# desired
1 + (
  2
)
# actual
1 + (
    2
)
```

Currently, the indention of parenthesis and operators such as `+` are summed up. Note that we
fixed the case of multiple parenthesis already (#68), i.e. their indention does not cumulate if they 
start on the same line.
```
((((
  1 # indented by one level
))))
```

title: support more indentions
description:
This PR is based on #29 to support more indention patterns.
The indention based on operators such as `+`, `-` etc. is different from the indention caused by brackets like `(`. In the latter case, the whole sub-expression has to be indented (that means everything until the closing brace occurs), whereas for the former, only the next token should be indented (if it is on a new line). Otherwise, the outcome looks like this:
```r
1 + 
  4 /
    5
```
But we want this:
```r
1 + 
  4 /
  5
```
Hence, I added a new column `spaces_before` that can take that into account. Not sure whether it can be solved differently (and more elegantly). The thing is that we need to strip end-of-line spaces since we build indention from scratch without taking into consideration the space between two tokens if they are separated by a line break. Therefore I think it is a reasonable solution.
I can rename `spaces` to `spaces_after` if you @krlmlr approve of this approach.

title: Fixing indention with multiple parenthesis
description:
This is supposed to be WIP and it's not yet optimised for performance. 

# Overview
* `indent_round()` and `indent_curly()` now first check (via `needs_indention()`) whether indention 
  is needed before they add it. The conditions are - loosely speaking - that there are not further
  indentions deeper in the nested structure that start on the same line. For the exact definition, I refer 
  to the help file of `needs_indention()`. This solves the first point brought up in #51, which is that
  multiple opening brackets on the same line should cause only one level of indention.

* `indent_round()` and `indent_curly()` now use `set_unindention_child()`, which sets the relative
  indention of closing token within children such as `{` and `(` to a negative number if necessary. This
  is necessary in cases where multiple closing brackets follow on the same line. In this case, an 
  additional closing bracket on a line causes the indention of the first bracket to become smaller (or 
  even zero). This addresses the second point brought up in #51. 

Consider the simple example:
```r
(((
  1
)))
```
The changes introduced by the first bullet above make sure that the indention of the innermost expression (which is `1`) is set to two spaces, the outer expressions don't feature any indention anymore. This means also that the closing brackets are unindented. The changes from the second bulled would not be necessary to make this simple example work.

Consider the more complicated example:
```r
call(
  call(
    16,
    5
))
```
The changes introduced by the second bullet above make sure the two closing brackets appear
right at the beginning of the line, with no spaces before them. Without the changes introduced by the second bullet above (but with the changes from the first bullet point), the expression `call(16, 5)` would be indented by two spaces (so would be the closing bracket of this expression). However, the closing bracket of this expression should not be indented since the last `)` of the whole example "undoes" the indention. To "undo" indention, we can assign a negative value (of two in this example) to the second last `)` and hence un-indent this very token (and consequentially, everything that follows on this line).

# To Do
* One change that was necessary due to the second bullet point was that `create_filler()` (which is
  called with the visitor on every level of nesting before anything else is done) cannot be used 
  anymore to set the indention level  (i.e. create the column indention) since we may have 
  manipulated it already when we were one level up since we set the indention of the children with
  `set_unindention_child()` (that is, `set_unindention_child()` affects not only the current level of
  nesting, but potentially also the children). That seems slightly suboptimal because now we need 
  to check in `create_filler()` and `set_unindention_child()` whether the column already exists.
* Regarding performance, maybe we can reduce the `which()` statements. Also, the `mutate()`
  statement in R/modify_pd.R#20 and the counterpart in `indent_curly()` may be moved into the 
  if-statment.

title: lorenzwalthert_medium
description:
In order to be consistent with `style_pkg()`, I used `withr::with_dir` to perform the styling. This, at the same time, means that the message printed (by `transform_lines_enc` internally) at the end of the styling to indicate which files were changed shows the paths relative to the *temporary* working directory used by `withr::with_dir` and not the directory that was the working directory before and after the execution of `style_src()`. If this is confusing, we have to do it without `withr::with_dir`, but then it would not be consistent anymore with `style_pkg()`, so I guess we can do it as proposed in this PR.

To increase the flexibility of the function regarding files in sub directories, `style_src()` has an argument `recursive` that will be passed to `dir` internally, so the user can choose whether to style files in just the selected directory or also in all sub-directories.
